items.title: Workflow spike: verify the eight Workflow API assumptions
items.action: In a `claude --plugin-dir plugins/harness` session, run a throwaway two-agent Workflow and record each answer, with what was observed, in docs/RESEARCH/pr-review/1016_workflow_spike.md. The probe agent is a throwaway, checkout-only plugins/harness/agents/spike-probe.md (tools Read and Write; its body Writes the value of ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} into its draft file). The published marketplace this repository's settings enable has no spike-probe, so its resolution shows which plugin root serves agentType: the spike note records the plugin root the probe echoed and the root scriptPath resolved from (checkout or installed cache). Answers: (1) scriptPath accepts a path under the plugin root; (2) a plugin-shipped workflows/ folder passes `claude plugin validate --strict`; (3) agentType 'harness:spike-probe' resolves to the checkout's agent (the echoed root names the checkout); (4) a workflow agent Writes its draft file without a permission prompt; (5) pipeline behavior when a stage returns null; (6) whether the Workflow call returns synchronously or asynchronously; (7) for Workflow agents, whether agent-watcher's turn.step, turn.complete and catch-all tool.call hooks fire with an agentId, what usage turn.step carries, and whether a Bash tool.call from a Workflow agent carries the same agentId (the slot binding TASK-9 uses under D6 watcher); (8) whether the output file's workflowProgress carries tokens, toolCalls, durationMs, label and model per agent (recorded for reference only: under D6 watcher no code reads the output file). The throwaway script, its workflows/ folder and spike-probe.md are removed after the run; nothing under plugins/ stays changed. TASK-5, TASK-6 and TASK-9 wait on this item.

PR_REVIEW.schema.json: $version 2.3.0; post_review_resolution.status gains REFUTED (closing: refuted by the findings refuter at build or by the developer through refute; evidence is the refuter's or the developer's case), BUBBLED (non-closing: a refutation overruled and routed to the bubble workflow) and NOT_RESOLVED (non-closing: overruled and routed to Phase 5 waves), with the description extended; verification_log.dispatch_time gains an optional adversarial_check object (applies, workflow, code_slots, refute_slots, result required, so {applies: true} alone is invalid; counts {findings_checked, findings_refuted, findings_upheld, code_findings}, refuted_ids, unrefuted_ids optional). review_merge: SCHEMA_VERSION 2.3.0; CLOSED_STATUSES gains only REFUTED. A new raw helper _entry_ids(resolutions) returns every id any resolution names, whatever its status; it backs the orphan check in compute_verdict (:351-353, with _bubbled_ids) and review_edit._disposed_ids (:307-310), so add_issue still skips those ids and merge_issue_ids still refuses a drop id with REFUTED then NOT_RESOLVED history. Only the disposition predicates follow the latest status: _named_ids names nothing for an id whose latest status is NOT_RESOLVED (REFUTED then NOT_RESOLVED is undispositioned; BUBBLED is named by the bubble entry the --bubble route writes), and _settled_ids (:333-337) drops an id whose latest status is NOT_RESOLVED even when bubbles or bubble_up still name it (a latest NOT_RESOLVED is open regardless of bubble entries), so undispositioned_ids, compute_verdict's pending set and review_edit.merge_issue_ids follow. _pending_problems exempts resolutions whose status is REFUTED, BUBBLED or NOT_RESOLVED (any other resolution or a READY verdict still fails). Hook validate_pr_json_schema.py: _incoherent gets the same exemption; _closeout_reason filters resolutions once at :236 (dropping REFUTED, BUBBLED and NOT_RESOLVED) and uses the filtered list in both the :244 clause (populated, not NOT READY, SHA evidence) and the :247 clause (no resolutions or SHA evidence), so a REFUTED entry's SHA-shaped evidence never clears a READY review. id_handling.all_issues_dispositioned (post-freeze addition, DesignEvolution S5) treats an id whose latest status is NOT_RESOLVED as open regardless of bubbles / bubble_up entries, the _settled_ids rule; disposition_ids stays as is, since pr_json_validation's orphan check reads it. review_edit.KNOWN_VERSIONS stays single-version ((rmg.SCHEMA_VERSION,), review_edit.py:56), so set_schema accepts only 2.3.0: tests/lib/test_review_edit.py:67 and :110 pin '2.2.0', and both literals become rmg.SCHEMA_VERSION (import review_merge as rmg there). schemas/README.md :31 and :33 name 2.3.0 (minor, no sweep); the pin in tests/lib/test_review_merge.py:404 moves to 2.3.0 and stays the one literal version pin (the planned tests compare with rmg.SCHEMA_VERSION or a (2, 3, 0) floor). review_edit.RESOLUTION_STATUSES gains none of the three, so resolve refuses them. items.title: review_merge traced merge, merge_adversarial, refuted key, review_document; review_edit overrules
items.action: review_merge.py: merge_findings_traced(reports) -> (issues, trace), trace mapping each issue id to its (source_id, finding_key) pairs; merge_findings stays and equals merge_findings_traced(...)[0]. merge_adversarial(reports, refutations) -> (issues, notes): merges every source (reviewer, code refuter, folded) through the trace; a finding with no refutation entry counts as upheld; an issue whose every finding is refuted carries 'refuted': <evidence>; in a mixed group rank, name, summary and fix_kind come from the upheld findings only and the refuted evidence goes to notes; with nothing refuted the issues equal merge_findings. _Record / _combine carry attack only to fold 'Attack: <text>' into the summary (D9). refuted_resolutions(issues, date) builds one REFUTED entry per refuted issue through _resolution; strip_refuted(issues) returns copies without the key. merge_ids (and regrade) carry refuted: kept only when every merged issue is refuted, evidence joined by a blank line. The spec's S5 rule holds for amend --merge too: in a mixed group (an issue dict without the refuted key is upheld) merge_ids orders the records upheld first before _combine, so the record that supplies the name and primary file is upheld, and takes the summary (_summary) and fix_kind (the judgment flag) from the upheld issues only; files, lines, fixes and reviewers still union over every merged issue, and the id (so the rank) stays keep's. review_document writes the refuted_resolutions, strips the key and computes the verdict over them (post_review_resolutions present only when non-empty, so TestReviewDocument.test_key_order_and_defaults keeps its key list; edit tests/lib/test_review_merge.py:399-404 only if the order must change). compute_verdict's READY text counts REFUTED ids apart: 'READY TO MERGE - <R> of <T> findings resolved, <B> bubbled' with R the closed ids that are not REFUTED, then ', <K> refuted' only when K > 0 (no suffix keeps every existing verdict string). review_edit.py: issue_info(doc, id) returns the issue dict or raises ValueError; apply_refute(doc, id, evidence, date) refuses an unknown id or a closing latest status (RESOLVED, CLOSED_NO_ACTION, REFUTED), appends a REFUTED entry and passes the result through _without_closed_bubbles, so a refuted bubbled id leaves the transient bubbles list; apply_unrefute(doc, id, mode, reason, date), mode bubble | fix, refuses unless the latest status is REFUTED (or an unknown mode / id); bubble appends BUBBLED and adds the id through add_bubble; fix appends NOT_RESOLVED and removes the id from the transient bubbles list. bubble_up is the terminal ledger (one {id, classification, reason} record per id), so both keep its entry as history, as resolve_all and _without_closed_bubbles already do; TASK-1's _settled_ids rule then counts the NOT_RESOLVED id open, so undispositioned_ids and the next waves see it. Both return a new doc with the verdict recomputed and never mutate the input. _without_closed_bubbles and merge_issue_ids treat REFUTED as closed through _closed_ids. decisions.question: How do matrix rows work for agents the Workflow tool dispatches (agent-watcher sees only Agent calls; tokens, tool_uses, duration_s are required integers)?

decisions.rationale: Developer, 2026-11-12: watcher is definitely preferred.
